anomalies.observed: Both MCP2515 CAN controllers are wired to the same SPI net set. U44 has SCK/SI/SO/CS on NET0178/NET0189/NET0186/NET0089, and U4 uses the identical labels, including the same chip-select net NET0089.
anomalies.expected: The specification calls for two CAN buses, each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller. Two SPI peripherals on the same bus must have separate chip-selects (or be on separate SPI buses) so the host can address them independently.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U44 ... 13 SCK NET0178, 14 SI NET0189, 15 SO NET0186, 16 CS NET0089
CAN BUS sheet: U4 ... 13 SCK NET0178, 14 SI NET0189, 15 SO NET0186, 16 CS NET0089
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)

anomalies.impact: The CM4 cannot select the two CAN controllers independently. When NET0089 is asserted, both MCP2515 devices are selected and can drive the SPI bus simultaneously, causing bus contention and preventing normal operation of both CAN interfaces.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers have both primary and secondary ground pins tied to the same board GND symbol: U2 pin 4 GND1 and pin 5 GND2 go to GND, and U29 pin 4 GND1 and pin 5 GND2 also go to GND.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN bus implemented with an isolated CAN transceiver should keep the CAN-side ground isolated from the board ground unless isolation is intentionally not used.

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of the CAN interfaces is defeated, allowing ground loops and removing the intended isolation between the rover and external CAN devices.
